cycles.trigger: Batch update-oldest-skills 2026-10-19: drift sweep (housing-deduction amendment in force 1.9.2026, nursing benefit 01.08.2026), live-checker audit, Judge + Expert + legal + holdout + value-add.
lessons: A regulation can be rewritten under a skill while its aggregator keeps the old table on the same page. Kol Zchut's housing page now leads with the 1.9.2026 table and keeps the old one below it headed 'old mechanism'; a snippet check that only looks for the old figure still PASSES. Search the page for 'החל מיום' / 'מנגנון חדש' before trusting a figure that is still present.

Seniority keys differ by entitlement, and a fix for one was nearly copied onto the other. Havraa runs on anniversary years of employment (year c+1 after c completed years), annual leave on CALENDAR years (Annual Leave Law s.1). The expert caught the leave mapping, which the author had 'fixed' by analogy with havraa.

The live checker had drifted from its own skill for two cycles: havraa zero in year one (the skill fixed that in 1.1.0), and 8 of its 9 goldens failed its own verify gate. Run the LIVE manifest through verify-checker-manifest.ts on every update, not just the regenerated one.
A calculator input that recovers a cost (the housing deduction) must also carry the cost itself, or the total can fall below the wage and an inflated expense lowers the answer.

Deferred (expert r2 minors): the back-pay row omits the rented-flat rate (508.62 Jerusalem) for January to August 2026; the wording 'no havraa tariff published for the year from 1.7.2026' should be re-checked; the scope of the 25% cap versus debts/advances (pre-existing, errs cautious). Resolved this cycle: the havraa 12-month condition and its bad-faith-dismissal exception.

Re-check on next update: the havraa tariff for the year from 1.7.2026 (unpublished as of 19.10.2026), the 1 January 2027 re-indexation of the housing ceilings and medical-insurance cap, and the January 2027 benefit and minimum-wage figures.

cycles.trigger: Full update-skill cycle: Independent Judge + expert employment-law review, two judge rounds, and the legal-review gate. Both gates FAILED round 1; three CRITICALs and seven round-2 regressions were fixed before push.
lessons: The worst defect was a TIMING error dressed as a cost fact: the skill said havraa is 'zero in year one'. Kol Zchut's own cited page says entitlement CRYSTALLISES at 12 months but is then paid retroactively from the first day. Eligibility and accrual are different clocks. A family following the old text reserved nothing for twelve months and then owed five days at once. The script reproduced the same error, so prose and tool were consistently wrong together. When a source says 'entitlement begins at X', ask separately what period the payment COVERS.

A dismissal timed just before a vesting date is a fact pattern the law anticipates. The exit table let a family read 'dismissed before completing one year' as a way to cap exposure at 12.5%. Severance Pay Law s.3 presumes exactly that dismissal was made to avoid severance. Any table keyed on 'before/after one year' needs the anti-avoidance rule beside it.

The coverage contract can outlive the correction it contradicts. references/domain-checklist.md still carried, as a TICKED must-cover item, the housing-deduction rule this skill retracted, attributed to the source that refutes it. The next cycle could have re-derived the wrong Step 4a from the checklist. Retracting a claim means editing the checklist in the same commit, not only the prose.

A stated rationale can be wrong even when the scope decision is right. The out-of-scope row justified excluding other sectors by claiming they ARE in the deposit fund; the deposit page lists agriculture, the experts sector and Palestinian workers as also exempt. Scope was still correct, for different reasons.

The remediation round introduced SEVEN new defects, found only because a second judge was run over the fixes. The sharpest: the Hebrew havraa gotcha was rewritten to say 'accrue from month one' but kept its old closing clause 'including it from month one inflates the cost', so the bullet argued both ways in the language most users read. A partial string replacement that leaves a trailing clause is invisible to every mechanical gate.

The English and Hebrew drifted asymmetrically. The uncited 'labour court supplements are higher than 20%' claim was removed from the Hebrew and from both Gotchas blocks but survived in English Step 3, and the Hebrew bundled-resources note listed fewer script guards than the English. Mirror parity has to be checked per CHANGED PASSAGE, not by heading count, which was 26/26 throughout.

Three reviewer-supplied facts had to be re-derived rather than transcribed. The 30-40% Gluten band could not be sourced from any primary text and was correctly left out; the only figure locatable anywhere (30%, ע"ע 1113/02) predates HCJ 1678/07, which removed the basis for a global supplement. Leaving a number out is a finding, not a gap.

kolzchut serves raw wikitext at ?action=raw and renders fine under plain curl, so the Playwright dependency of earlier cycles was unnecessary. But snippets quoted from the RAW wikitext fail --check-sources, because template markup and transcluded data-pages ({{נתון:דמי הבראה פרטי}}) do not appear in rendered text. Quote the RENDERED page; use raw only to locate.

A derived number fails the evidence gate even when it is arithmetically right. The (wage x 4% + hourly) x 1.5 formula is template markup, but the rendered page publishes its RESULT, 439.73, verbatim. Citing the published figure instead of the formula both satisfied the gate and closed an executability gap, since worked holidays carry the same amount.

The published skill had NO legal notice in either language and the structural gate had been reporting regulated level=3 the whole time. The gate only fires when someone runs it. Classification came out Tier B (S2 x F1): the skill reaches a shekel conclusion about the user's own household and a severance conclusion on their contemplated act, but holds itself out as nothing, drafts no reserved instrument, and routes the global-supplement question to a lawyer.

The checker manifest carried disclaimerKey 'benefits' when the tool computes an employer's payroll exposure and permitted wage deductions. That is employment, and the notice rendered above the calculate button was therefore the wrong domain's. Fixed on both DBs.

The calculator's 25% cap branch is unreachable with only the three heads it models (max 552.32 against a 1,610.96 cap), so printing 'X of Y requested against the cap' read as clearance to deduct more. Over-deduction is a criminal offence, so the tool now says explicitly which heads it does NOT model and that the headroom is not clearance.

A cross-field consistency check written in one direction is half a check. --month 3 with --completed-years 1 was rejected while --month 30 with --completed-years 0 sailed through and costed havraa at the first-year rate for a two-year worker.

Executability held without the shell. Four declared hosts cannot run python; every constant is in prose and a hand computation reproduces the script byte for byte (7,819.79 gross, 2,363.79 net at level 5). The one head that was unreachable by hand, a worked holiday, is now a published figure rather than an instruction to go look it up.

cycles.trigger: Review-round evidence-integrity pass; the new --check-sources gate flagged 7 of 25 snippets as absent from their cited URLs.
lessons: ALL 7 flagged figures verified CORRECT against live sources (care levels 1,705/2,480/3,472/...6,448 at 01.04.2026; severance one month per year; BL employer 3.6%; havraa 5/6/7 by seniority; vacation gross 16/18/21; two employment routes; no statutory overtime by Supreme Court case law). They failed the gate only because kolzchut and BTL are JS-rendered, so the curl-based check saw nav chrome. Re-anchored all 7 with verified_via:browser.

PROCESS LESSON (my error): I mis-stated the skill's vacation claim when briefing the research agent ('1-4=14, 5=16, 6=18'), and the agent correctly found THAT string mixes net+gross. But the skill actually uses the gross column consistently (yrs 1-5=16, yr 6=18, yr 7=21) and is correct. Always check the agent's premise against the actual file before acting on a 'WRONG' verdict.

Two dead-ish citations corrected: severance rule verbatim is on the 'fired/employer-died' zchuton, not the 'resigned' one; benefit amounts are on the per-level BTL pages (level1/2/3/6.aspx), not the ovedZar landing page. Levels 2/3/6 are hours-per-week x 248 NIS, not printed as lump sums.
The '3.6% from January 2025' effective date could not be confirmed on any source; the rate 3.6% is correct, so the date was dropped from the evidence claim (body already states just the rate).
Checker foreign-caregiver-cost uses the BL rate and benefit levels, both confirmed correct, so NO regeneration needed.
kolzchut/BTL are JS-rendered: the gate reports their snippets as FAILED under curl. Use verified_via:browser after a real render; do not treat a curl FAILED on these hosts as a wrong figure.
